bull_bear.body: Regulatory risks, competition from other entertainment companies
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Imagicaa World has a strong brand presence in India, with a focus on providing unique entertainment experiences
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Majority-stake-plus-fee model for new assets: Rs 50 Crores for 50.002% of the Mehsana SPV, with the company also partnering existing owners to expand the park's offerings while undertaking O&M and earning management fees of 6%-10%.
- Asset-light preference for the new indoor vertical (leased in-city FECs, partner-supplied hardware, software and training) alongside the land-heavy owned outdoor parks.
- Growth funding context flagged by the deck: state tourism policies offering fiscal incentives - Maharashtra (2016), Gujarat (2021-2025, capital subsidy and electricity duty exemption for parks with investment >INR 500 mn), Tamil Nadu (2023, projects over minimum 15 acres) and Madhya Pradesh (2016).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Location advantage: the park sits off the Mumbai - Pune Expressway on a large parcel of land owned by the Company, which together with international-quality rides and a qualified operations team is described as a significant competitive advantage over any new park
- Established 'Imagicaa' brand recognition in Mumbai, Pune, the rest of Maharashtra and Gujarat, built through superior visitor experience and word-of-mouth recall
- School-group focus, where visiting school children act as brand ambassadors with potential to bring the family back on another visit
- Dynamic and attractive pricing that flexes with events, festivals, seasons and holidays through the year
- Promoter backing from the Malpani Group, a diversified house with more than 18 years of experience in park operations as well as project expertise
- Senior management team of media, entertainment, marketing and consumer executives with an average tenure of more than 15 years in such industries
- Consolidation of the group's park business under a single umbrella, expected to optimise sales, reduce cost and increase profitability
- High operating leverage on a relatively fixed cost base, so incremental attendance and per-capita spend flow through to profitability
- Structured safety and security infrastructure - dedicated command centre, zoned perimeters, third-party maintenance audits, TUV SUD South Asia inspection and certification, an on-site medical centre and ambulances
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Seasonality and weather dependence — The theme and water park industry is seasonal. Attendance is volatile with school vacations, public holidays, weekends and adverse weather such as excessive heat and monsoons; the water park earns higher revenue in summer while the monsoon months reduce revenue. This is not theoretical for the Company - FY26 standalone visitors fell to 23.0 Lakhs, down about 15% from FY 2024-25, because an early and elongated monsoon hit the high peak season.
- Dependence on discretionary consumer spending and changing consumer tastes — Success depends substantially on consumer tastes and preferences that change in often unpredictable ways, and on discretionary spending, which is heavily influenced by general economic conditions and disposable income. Difficult economic conditions or inflationary periods can reduce attendance, visit frequency and per-capita spend - both of which management identifies as key drivers of revenue and profitability.
- Safety incidents and adverse publicity damaging the brand — Brands and reputation are among the Company's most important assets. Park operation carries the risk of accidents, contagious, airborne or waterborne diseases and other incidents that could damage guest perception of safety, health and security. Product quality and safety is flagged in the BRSR material-issues table, where mishaps, falls, fatalities and injuries could attract fines, penalties and legal or regulatory liabilities.
- Epidemic and pandemic exposure — Identified as a newer risk for the industry. Theme parks operate in a highly crowded environment where physical distancing is difficult, and regulators have targeted the industry for restrictions by categorising it a 'non-essential' service.
- Customer experience and satisfaction dependence — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications. Customer satisfaction drives reputation at a base level; an unsatisfactory guest experience may pose a risk to business continuity, while positive experiences drive revisits and word-of-mouth that reduces marketing cost.
- Energy intensity and energy-sourcing risk — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications. The hospitality and entertainment parks industry is typically energy-intensive because energy is required to run rides, lighting, fireworks and other facilities; decisions on energy intensity and energy sources affect operating efficiency and the risk profile.
- Water and waste management, and environmental compliance — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications. Improper waste handling may contribute to air pollution and climate change, cause health and safety risks to exposed personnel, and non-compliance with waste management regulations may lead to heavy fines.
- Employee well-being, training and retention — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk. A high attrition rate signals low employee satisfaction to investors, and lack of training or experience puts employees at risk in a safety-critical ride-operations environment; retention also affects hiring and onboarding cost.
- Geographic and asset concentration — The business is anchored on a single flagship destination off the Mumbai - Pune Expressway, with brand recognition concentrated in Mumbai, Pune, the rest of Maharashtra and Gujarat. Diversification into Madhya Pradesh and into indoor formats is only beginning, so a shock to the flagship location or its catchment is structurally material.
- Related-party concentration and governance controls — The Company transacts extensively with entities controlled by KMP - including acquisition of a business undertaking and of the Mandrup solar plant from Giriraj Enterprises, a partnership firm in which directors and their relatives are partners - and operates under a promoter holding company. Separately, the audit trail (edit log) feature was not enabled throughout the year for a frontend software for the park business and at the database level for two accounting software at the Holding Company, and for one subsidiary.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Headline platform scale: "8 Owned Parks + 1 under O&M", "1 5-Star Hotel in Khopoli", "2 Hello Park LOIs Signed" and "6+ Cities Covered", grouped into Mumbai-Pune (4 parks), Rest of Maharashtra (2), Gujarat (2) and Central India (1).
- Catchment advantage claimed as ~37mn population across MMR + Pune served by Khopoli-Lonavala, ~15mn across Surat, Sabarmati & Ahmedabad, and ~8mn across Indore, Ujjain & Dewas.
- Difficult-to-replicate footprint: established presence in key Western India markets, "Large land parcels + high upfront capex create significant entry barriers", and first-mover advantage in several high-potential catchments.
- "One Platform, Multiple Entertainment Formats" with "150+ rides & attractions across the portfolio" spanning amusement, theme, water, devotional and indoor kids entertainment.
- Differentiated assets cited: Sai Teerth is described as India's first devotional theme park dedicated to Sai Baba with the first animatronic humanoid of Sai Baba, and Wet'n Joy Lonavala as India's largest water park by ride and water body capacity.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Investment in Mehsana Next Parks Pvt. Ltd. (Shanku's Water Park, Gujarat's largest water park per the deck) - Rs 50 Crores for 50.002%; rationale cites strong regional brand recall, a recently renovated ride portfolio, and land available for future expansion.
- [Partnership] Hello Park is described as the "World's largest chain of immersive, digital-physical (phygital) parks for children, with 50+ locations globally"; Imagicaa has secured exclusive rights for India to roll out the format nationwide.
- [Industry] Crisil-sourced outlook: Indian entertainment park market size of INR 108-114 bn in FY24E rising to INR 190-200 bn by FY30E at a 9-11% CAGR (FY18: 68, FY23: 105, 8% CAGR over that period), with domestic tourist visits projected at 3,500 mn by CY30P at a 9% CAGR.
- [Leadership] Promoter (Malpani) family holds Chairman (Rajesh Malpani, Non-Executive), Managing Director (Jai Malpani) and Non-Executive Director (Manish Malpani) roles; CEO and CMO Dhimant Bakshi has been associated with IEL since 2012 and CFO & Head-Legal Mayuresh Kore since 2009.
- [Entry barriers] The deck leans on Crisil's stated barriers - capital intensity, land acquisition hurdles (typical large parks need around 30-50 acres), lack of differentiated offerings among smaller players, and executional/operational expertise with longer break-even periods.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company runs destination-based out-of-home entertainment assets - a theme park and water park with associated food & beverage, retail and merchandise operations, plus a hotel positioned as a destination for entertainment, corporate meetings, off-sites and social events. Revenue is driven by park attendance (admission tickets) and by per-capita non-ticketing spend on F&B, retail and sponsorship. Following the consolidation of the group's park business under a single umbrella and its foray into the Hello Park indoor entertainment concept, the Company is diversifying beyond destination outdoor parks into scalable, asset-light, all-weather formats.

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Expansion into new markets, introduction of new attractions
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expand into newer geographies by leveraging the Imagicaa brand, having already entered Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, with FY26 marking the full year of operations of Aqua Imagicaa water park in Indore
- Diversify beyond destination-based outdoor parks into the indoor amusement segment through the Hello Park concept - a scalable, asset-light, all-weather format
- Grow park attendance through media and marketing campaigns aimed at families, school groups, college students, young professionals and corporates, and through outreach in secondary catchments such as Delhi NCR, Bangalore, Hyderabad and Jaipur
- Adopt a dynamic pricing model that adjusts admission prices by expected demand and coincides with events, festivals, seasons and holidays
- Diversify revenue streams away from admission tickets by growing F&B and retail/merchandise per-capita spend, selling sponsorship and ride naming rights, and using the hotel to position Imagicaa for corporate meetings, off-sites and social events
- Leverage the Company's own brands and characters as an intellectual property portfolio to develop new media and entertainment options and consumer-product sales
- Improve profitability through cost optimisation - economies of scale, company-wide centralised procurement and sourcing, integrated marketing campaigns and shared services across security, ticketing, F&B and general administration
- Consolidate the group's park business under a single umbrella to optimise sales, reduce common cost and create scale for expansion into other states nationally and internationally
- Secure renewable power for the parks, including an open access agreement for 8 MW of solar and wind energy and the acquisition of a solar power undertaking at Mandrup, Solapur
- Pursue inorganic expansion through SPVs and joint ventures, such as the approved investment in Mehsana Next Parks Private Limited with Keshav Holiday Resort Private Limited
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion in FY26 was directed at new geographies and new formats rather than at capacity additions in the existing park. The Company has ventured into Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, and FY26 marked the full year of operations of Aqua Imagicaa water park in Indore, a city the Company identifies within the Indore-Ujjain tourism and growth corridor. It has entered the indoor amusement segment through its foray into Hello Park, a globally recognised indoor entertainment concept described as a scalable, asset-light and all-weather format that diversifies the Company beyond destination-based outdoor parks. On the entity side, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Imagicaa Next Private Limited, on June 16, 2025, and as on the date of signing of the Board's Report the Board had approved an investment in Mehsana Next Parks Private Limited, a proposed SPV/joint venture with Keshav Holiday Resort Private Limited, to carry on an existing water park and develop a proposed amusement park (Shanku's Water Park). On the energy side the Company is acquiring a solar power undertaking at Mandrup, Solapur with generation of 6.65 MW, to be primarily utilised for parks it owns and operates, under a related-party arrangement capped at not exceeding Rs 16.00 Crore across FY 2024-25 and/or FY 2025-26; separately (per the BRSR material-issues table routed to the risks_esg bundle of the same annual report) an open access power agreement has been secured for procurement of 8 MW of renewable energy from solar and wind sources, which currently meets over 60% of the park's total energy requirements. The Board declined a dividend for FY26 expressly to retain funds for the acquisition transactions and expansions undertaken by the Company. The Company also received an Eligibility Certificate from the Department of Tourism, Government of Maharashtra for its hotel business operated as Novotel Imagicaa, with an incentive period from 1st November 2024 to 31st October 2034.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Post-COVID demand for experiential outdoor entertainment has been rising and footfall of all major parks has reached pre-pandemic levels
- Demand for theme and water parks is expected to increase in India over the next few years, driven by increasing disposable income, favourable demographics, changing consumer preferences, growing affinity towards experiences, and a dearth of outdoor entertainment activities in cities
- State governments are recognising the potential of amusement parks and working with industry to implement conducive policies; several states offer capital subsidies in the range of 15-25% along with land facilitation and faster approvals under tourism policies
- Underlying consumption trends, particularly in discretionary and experiential segments, remain structurally intact, providing a supportive backdrop for leisure and entertainment
- Rising share of discretionary spending in household consumption, supported by a young demographic profile, urbanisation, improved connectivity, digital penetration and social-media influence
- Tier I and Tier II cities alike are emerging as key growth markets, with expansion increasingly directed toward Tier II and Tier III clusters where land costs are often 60-70% below metro levels
- India's indoor amusement industry is valued at approximately INR 15,000 crore per an ANAROCK and IAAPI report, with spending on indoor amusement experiences up 30-40% versus pre-pandemic levels
- India's amusement park industry is estimated at approximately USD 640 million (~Rs 5,300 crore) in 2025 and projected to reach ~USD 1.1-1.2 billion by 2033, a CAGR of around 7-8%
- The industry constantly needs to innovate and introduce fresh themes and experiences, and to focus on stronger marketing strategies to draw a larger audience
- Near-term risk that elevated inflation, particularly from higher energy and food prices, moderates discretionary spending, and that volatility in travel patterns affects footfall at destination formats
- FY26 performance was hit by an early and elongated monsoon that impacted the high peak season, with standalone visitors of 23.0 Lakhs, down ~15% from FY 2024-25
- Indian GDP growth is projected to moderate to 6.6% in FY27 as geopolitical uncertainty and higher energy prices weigh on demand
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY26 was directed at new geographies and new formats rather than at capacity additions in the existing park. The Company has ventured into Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, and FY26 marked the full year of operations of Aqua Imagicaa water park in Indore, a city the Company identifies within the Indore-Ujjain tourism and growth corridor. It has entered the indoor amusement segment through its foray into Hello Park, a globally recognised indoor entertainment concept described as a scalable, asset-light and all-weather format that diversifies the Company beyond destination-based outdoor parks. On the entity side, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Imagicaa Next Private Limited, on June 16, 2025, and as on the date of signing of the Board's Report the Board had approved an investment in Mehsana Next Parks Private Limited, a proposed SPV/joint venture with Keshav Holiday Resort Private Limited, to carry on an existing water park and develop a proposed amusement park (Shanku's Water Park). On the energy side the Company is acquiring a solar power undertaking at Mandrup, Solapur with generation of 6.65 MW, to be primarily utilised for parks it owns and operates, under a related-party arrangement capped at not exceeding Rs 16.00 Crore across FY 2024-25 and/or FY 2025-26; separately (per the BRSR material-issues table routed to the risks_esg bundle of the same annual report) an open access power agreement has been secured for procurement of 8 MW of renewable energy from solar and wind sources, which currently meets over 60% of the park's total energy requirements. The Board declined a dividend for FY26 expressly to retain funds for the acquisition transactions and expansions undertaken by the Company. The Company also received an Eligibility Certificate from the Department of Tourism, Government of Maharashtra for its hotel business operated as Novotel Imagicaa, with an incentive period from 1st November 2024 to 31st October 2034.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company runs destination-based out-of-home entertainment assets - a theme park and water park with associated food & beverage, retail and merchandise operations, plus a hotel positioned as a destination for entertainment, corporate meetings, off-sites and social events. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Post-COVID demand for experiential outdoor entertainment has been rising and footfall of all major parks has reached pre-pandemic levels
- Demand for theme and water parks is expected to increase in India over the next few years, driven by increasing disposable income, favourable demographics, changing consumer preferences, growing affinity towards experiences, and a dearth of outdoor entertainment activities in cities
- State governments are recognising the potential of amusement parks and working with industry to implement conducive policies; several states offer capital subsidies in the range of 15-25% along with land facilitation and faster approvals under tourism policies
- Underlying consumption trends, particularly in discretionary and experiential segments, remain structurally intact, providing a supportive backdrop for leisure and entertainment
- Rising share of discretionary spending in household consumption, supported by a young demographic profile, urbanisation, improved connectivity, digital penetration and social-media influence
- Tier I and Tier II cities alike are emerging as key growth markets, with expansion increasingly directed toward Tier II and Tier III clusters where land costs are often 60-70% below metro levels
- India's indoor amusement industry is valued at approximately INR 15,000 crore per an ANAROCK and IAAPI report, with spending on indoor amusement experiences up 30-40% versus pre-pandemic levels
- India's amusement park industry is estimated at approximately USD 640 million (~Rs 5,300 crore) in 2025 and projected to reach ~USD 1.1-1.2 billion by 2033, a CAGR of around 7-8%
- The industry constantly needs to innovate and introduce fresh themes and experiences, and to focus on stronger marketing strategies to draw a larger audience
- Near-term risk that elevated inflation, particularly from higher energy and food prices, moderates discretionary spending, and that volatility in travel patterns affects footfall at destination formats
- FY26 performance was hit by an early and elongated monsoon that impacted the high peak season, with standalone visitors of 23.0 Lakhs, down ~15% from FY 2024-25
- Indian GDP growth is projected to moderate to 6.6% in FY27 as geopolitical uncertainty and higher energy prices weigh on demand

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion in FY26 was directed at new geographies and new formats rather than at capacity additions in the existing park. The Company has ventured into Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, and FY26 marked the full year of operations of Aqua Imagicaa water park in Indore, a city the Company identifies within the Indore-Ujjain tourism and growth corridor. It has entered the indoor amusement segment through its foray into Hello Park, a globally recognised indoor entertainment concept described as a scalable, asset-light and all-weather format that diversifies the Company beyond destination-based outdoor parks. On the entity side, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Imagicaa Next Private Limited, on June 16, 2025, and as on the date of signing of the Board's Report the Board had approved an investment in Mehsana Next Parks Private Limited, a proposed SPV/joint venture with Keshav Holiday Resort Private Limited, to carry on an existing water park and develop a proposed amusement park (Shanku's Water Park). On the energy side the Company is acquiring a solar power undertaking at Mandrup, Solapur with generation of 6.65 MW, to be primarily utilised for parks it owns and operates, under a related-party arrangement capped at not exceeding Rs 16.00 Crore across FY 2024-25 and/or FY 2025-26; separately (per the BRSR material-issues table routed to the risks_esg bundle of the same annual report) an open access power agreement has been secured for procurement of 8 MW of renewable energy from solar and wind sources, which currently meets over 60% of the park's total energy requirements. The Board declined a dividend for FY26 expressly to retain funds for the acquisition transactions and expansions undertaken by the Company. The Company also received an Eligibility Certificate from the Department of Tourism, Government of Maharashtra for its hotel business operated as Novotel Imagicaa, with an incentive period from 1st November 2024 to 31st October 2034.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Location advantage: the park sits off the Mumbai - Pune Expressway on a large parcel of land owned by the Company, which together with international-quality rides and a qualified operations team is described as a significant competitive advantage over any new park
- Established 'Imagicaa' brand recognition in Mumbai, Pune, the rest of Maharashtra and Gujarat, built through superior visitor experience and word-of-mouth recall
- School-group focus, where visiting school children act as brand ambassadors with potential to bring the family back on another visit
- Dynamic and attractive pricing that flexes with events, festivals, seasons and holidays through the year
- Promoter backing from the Malpani Group, a diversified house with more than 18 years of experience in park operations as well as project expertise
- Senior management team of media, entertainment, marketing and consumer executives with an average tenure of more than 15 years in such industries
- Consolidation of the group's park business under a single umbrella, expected to optimise sales, reduce cost and increase profitability
- High operating leverage on a relatively fixed cost base, so incremental attendance and per-capita spend flow through to profitability
- Structured safety and security infrastructure - dedicated command centre, zoned perimeters, third-party maintenance audits, TUV SUD South Asia inspection and certification, an on-site medical centre and ambulances

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory risks, competition from other entertainment companies

non_obvious.body: Imagicaa World has a strong brand presence in India, with a focus on providing unique entertainment experiences

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand into newer geographies by leveraging the Imagicaa brand, having already entered Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, with FY26 marking the full year of operations of Aqua Imagicaa water park in Indore
- Diversify beyond destination-based outdoor parks into the indoor amusement segment through the Hello Park concept - a scalable, asset-light, all-weather format
- Grow park attendance through media and marketing campaigns aimed at families, school groups, college students, young professionals and corporates, and through outreach in secondary catchments such as Delhi NCR, Bangalore, Hyderabad and …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Investment in Mehsana Next Parks Pvt. Ltd. (Shanku's Water Park, Gujarat's largest water park per the deck) - Rs 50 Crores for 50.002%; rationale cites strong regional brand recall, a recently renovated ride portfolio, and land available for future expansion.
- [Partnership] Hello Park is described as the "World's largest chain of immersive, digital-physical (phygital) parks for children, with 50+ locations globally"; Imagicaa has secured exclusive rights for India to roll out the format nationwide.
- [Industry] Crisil-sourced outlook: Indian entertainment park market size of INR 108-114 bn in FY24E rising to INR 190-200 bn by FY30E at a 9-11% CAGR (FY18: 68, FY23: 105, 8% CAGR over that period), with domestic tourist visits projected at 3,500 mn by CY30P at a 9% CAGR.
- [Leadership] Promoter (Malpani) family holds Chairman (Rajesh Malpani, Non-Executive), Managing Director (Jai Malpani) and Non-Executive Director (Manish Malpani) roles; CEO and CMO Dhimant Bakshi has been associated with IEL since 2012 and CFO & Head-Legal Mayuresh Kore since 2009.
- [Entry barriers] The deck leans on Crisil's stated barriers - capital intensity, land acquisition hurdles (typical large parks need around 30-50 acres), lack of differentiated offerings among smaller players, and executional/operational expertise with longer break-even periods.
